newsitem.title: UK: GUS buys U.S. information firm Experian.
newsitem.headline: GUS buys U.S. information firm Experian.

text.p: Britain's Great Universal Stores Plc said on Thursday that it has bought Experian in a deal that values the U.S. credit, marketing and real estate information services company at $1.7 billion on a debt free basis.
The British retailer said that its existing European information services business CCN will be merged with Experian.

Experian, based in Orange County, California, has three proprietary databases -- consumers, businesses and real estate -- with information on over 190 million people and 91 million households in the U.S.

Once part of TRW Inc, an 80.4 percent stake in Eperian was acquired in February this year by a Bain Capital Inc unit, Thomas H Lee Co and other investors. Eperian generated sales of $540 million in 1995 and pro forma profit of $109 million.

GUS has put in place an $800 million five-year term loan and the rest of the deal will be financed from its existing cash resources. GUS said the move was expected to enhance earnings in the first full year and to generate strong cash flow.

"Together, the two operations (Eperian and CCN) are very well placed to develop new business opportunities and, in particular, to provide global solutions to large multinational clients," GUS chairman Lord Wolfson said. GUS shares were indicated up 20 pence ($0.33) at 610-1/2 following the news. ($1=.6054 Pound)
